segments.source: This is a US whole-bean shortlist for an automatic filter brewer making several cups at once. We required an exact currently identifiable bag, an explicit roaster statement about automatic drip, a linked full Coffeedant review and a distinct buyer reason. We excluded a coffee whose only method evidence was a hand-pour recipe, and we did not rank a sold-out or unclear format by price.
segments.context: This is a US whole-bean shortlist for an automatic filter brewer making several cups at once. We required an exact currently identifiable bag, an explicit roaster statement about automatic drip, a linked full Coffeedant review and a distinct buyer reason. We excluded a coffee whose only method evidence was a hand-pour recipe, and we did not rank a sold-out or unclear format by price. [1] [3] [4]

segments.source: The choice is between a nutty daily medium blend, a brighter medium blend and a darker chocolate-rich blend that can take cream. All three roasters describe their own intended flavor. Those descriptions do not prove what a future bag will taste like in your machine. Coffeedant has not bought or brewed these bags.

segments.source: Our espresso-and-drip guide solves a different problem: one bag and grinder moving between a portafilter and a filter brewer. This page assumes the pot is the main job. That changes the questions to basket capacity, repeated full-carafe use, whether the household drinks black or with cream, and how quickly a larger bag will be consumed.

segments.source: The SCA home-brewer requirement uses about 55 g of coffee per liter at maximum capacity to check that a basket accommodates a full brew without overflow. That is a design requirement for certified equipment, not a universal best dose for your coffee. Stumptown’s 28 g to 475 ml drip start is close to 59 g/L. Counter Culture gives a wider general filter range of one part coffee to 15–18 parts water. Keep your machine manual, actual water fill and basket limit in view.

That is a design requirement for certified equipment, not a universal best dose for your coffee. Stumptown’s 28 g to 475 ml drip start is close to 59 g/L. Counter Culture gives a wider general filter range of one part coffee to 15–18 parts water. Keep your machine manual, actual water fill and basket limit in view. [2] [3] [6]

segments.source: Start with one weighed coffee and water amount, the same filter, and a grind appropriate to your machine. Brew a full pot only if the brewer and basket are designed for it. Record the result before changing grind or dose. If a pot tastes weak after sitting, first distinguish brew strength from time on a warming plate; beans cannot fix an overheld carafe. None of these suggestions is a Coffeedant extraction measurement.

segments.source: Blue Bottle’s 27 g to 350 g recipe is explicitly for its hand-poured dripper. It helps identify the roaster’s filter-coffee intent but should not be entered as an automatic-brewer preset. A machine controls delivery differently, and its basket may use a different filter geometry.

segments.source: Fast Forward is the restrained starting point when several drinkers prefer a familiar nutty and sweet direction. Counter Culture says the underlying coffees rotate, so the roast-date selector matters more than an old country list. The Guardian’s prior sample is an independent opinion about that sample, not a calibration for the bag sold today.

segments.source: Holler Mountain introduces a stated citrus and berry-jam direction over caramel. Stumptown says it serves daily drip and publishes a practical starting dose. That makes it the clearest recipe-led first try if the household accepts a bit of brightness. Its medium-roast label does not guarantee that everyone will perceive the same acidity.

segments.source: Bella Donovan is the dark option when black coffee or cream is the routine. Blue Bottle describes chocolate, raspberry and molasses, and says the blend holds up in automatic drip. An older independent tasting can illustrate one earlier bag, but the roaster’s current listing is the evidence for today’s identity and intent. Do not interpret “dark” as “fruit-free.”

A direct listing does not verify the date or storage history of the bag delivered to you.
